posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Working as intended, per the Steam FAQ point 7:

  • If the Chairman is destroyed before the Operative then the Chairman enters the trash pile (unlike Omnitron who's removed from the the game when defeated), meaning that there can be 26 cards in the villain deck at that point.

    It also means that the Chairman can be played after the villain deck is reshuffled effectively undoing your hard work.

posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
Mint. I think the environment probably did more damage than anything else...and almost all of it to the Operative and the Organization, since I got Environmental Allies out and the Naturalist went Gazelle. I was a bit worried when an early major underboss turn got a nasty Contract set up, but I ended up having a few turns to turtle and even heal when Immutus was out and soaking up so much damage thanks to EA and...whichever Endling reduces damage to environment targets. Eventually I clawed back out (Tiger Clawed, you might say, as that and Dual Crowbars turned Fixer into the prime mover of damage). Naturalist using Blend into the Pack also helped him not take any damage on first attack (there were something like ten environmental targets out).

Parse was primarily useful for Extrasensory Awareness--I tossed one Prison Break that way, which definitely helped--and Bunker was mostly extra damage with Flak/Maintenance and Turret Mode.

 

Started out worried, ended feeling like a slog. Not least just because there were so many environment cards out, and none of them was dealing any damage to anything. (Chairman, EA.)

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
Mint.  Mine was much more sloggy than most people's, it sounds like.   I got a nasty Prison Break right after I flipped the Chairman, and before I could get out Extrasensory Awareness to stop it.  The Chairman/Contract/Hired Gun combo really knocked me down, and it took a lucky Immutus soon after that to bring me back.  Between that and Naturalist in Gazelle with Environmental Allies, it took quite a while for the Chairman's goons to take down Immutus.   

 

For the last 3-4 turns of the game, basically every environment card was in play, but couldn't hurt me.  Slowly, I built everybody up -- Naturalist spent the whole rest of the game in Gazelle, healing 3HP per round; the plethora of environment cards meant that Run with the Pack was a -11DR, so because Naturalist had the highest HP, any henchman could be killed without fear of reprisal from the Operative.  Parse had double Exploit Vulnerabilities, plus Extrasensory Awareness, Buffer Overflow and Segmentation Fault, so the Chairman's deck was under control.   Fixer had Pipe Wrench and Driving Mantis, which meant he could hit the Chairman, and redirect the retaliation damage to the Operative (while she lived).  Bunker got hit the hardest by the bad Prison Break.  His first three card plays were Flak Cannon, Maintenance Unit and Turret Mode, and he spent the entire rest of the game healing 2 and dealing 3 damage.  

 

In a slow, painful, careful grind, The Operative went down first, then Fixer switched to Dual Crowbars, and took out the Chairman on a Parse/Between-the-Lines-induced out-of-turn hit.  Final HP:  Fixer-7 Parse-7 Naturalist-18 Bunker-12

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Near mint.  Despite Parse's best efforts, two poorly-timed Prison Breaks were just... yuck.  It was pretty close, but these guys have some useless incap abilities, so once it starts going south, it's just a downward spiral.

As an aside, has The Operative been errata'ed multiple times now?  I happened to play against the Chairman this last weekend, and her Oversized card says, "When the Operative is destroyed..." (I forget the rest, I don't have it in front of me right now.)  However, her digital version says, "When the Operative would be destroyed, her character card flips instead" and the full cards breakdowns spreadsheet says, "When The Operative is reduced to 0 or fewer HP, flip The Operative's Character card."  The video game version is correct, of course (per a Fireside Chat), but man, that's a mess.  Since we were playing with Haka and the Temple of Zhu Long, the difference was highly pertinent.

And another comment: If the Chairman is oversized, clearly he physically can't get shuffled into the villain deck, so you have to haul out his normal-sized cards.  But he has two of those!  I guess the canonical way to play is that one card goes in the villain trash and the other just floats around?  Having both go in would be totally unplayable.  But only one card goes in the trash, the other would remain on his Chairman Pike side!  Do you just pretend it doesn't exist?  That's really confusing.
